acceptance.notes: Could not construct an e2e reproduction that fails before/passes after this specific fix: the modal's own content (5 short fields) never gets tall enough to exercise .modal-body's max-height:90vh bound, and CSS Flexbox's automatic-minimum-size rule already zeroes min-height on a flex item whose relevant-axis overflow is auto (not clip) — unlike main's clip case, .modal-body's overflow-y:auto likely already got min-height:0 for free. Fixed anyway per the task's explicit instruction (T347 flagged it, comments-and-pairs only, left for this migration to actually fix) and per ADR-0041 §4's own closing sentence ('state it rather than inheriting it').

risks.risk: hub ADR-0042 §2's headPinned/footPinned mechanism silently breaks main's fixed-header clearance when headPinned is set on a route whose screen registers no *appScreenHead template. main's own [class.after-head] (private-layout.html) drops the 52px fixed-header margin-top whenever chrome().headPinned is truthy, on the unstated assumption that a registered *appScreenHead always supplies that clearance itself via .screen-head's own margin-top. config-manager has nothing natural to project as a head, so an initial headPinned:true attempt stranded every interactive element under the fixed app-screen-header (reproduced: 8/10 new spec cases failed, every .pill/.rail-item click intercepted). footPinned:true achieves the same scroll-ownership yield (pinned() is headPinned || footPinned) without the clearance coupling, and was used instead — but this is a workaround, not a documented supported path, and nothing in ADR-0042 says a screen may pin without registering a template, or that footPinned is the safe choice for it.
risks.surfaces_at: T343's seating-plan PR is the immediate exposure: ADR-0042 §Context ¶2 / T343's own corrected acceptance text instructs 'headPinned: true on its route, screen-scroll() outside any respond-to()' for seating-plan, and seating-plan.html currently registers no *appScreenHead or *appScreenFoot either (grep confirmed, 2026-09-04) — following that instruction literally will very likely reproduce this exact regression. milestones is a second candidate for the same trap once its own migration reaches route data. Worth a hub ADR-0042 amendment (or an explicit T343 correction) stating the headPinned/footPinned choice depends on whether a head/foot is actually registered, not just on which single-scroller effect is wanted.

decisions_needed.question: config-manager.scss is 16.81 kB against an 8 kB anyComponentStyle budget, and a correct, complete layout-layer migration only moved it from 16.78 kB — the gap is not scroll/shell CSS. How should the remaining ~8.8 kB be closed, given T344 depends on all four T343 screens being under budget?
options: Extract the local 'add couple member' modal (.modal-overlay/.modal-dialog/.modal-header/.modal-body/.modal-footer and its ~15 form-field rules, roughly a fifth of the file by rule count) into its own standalone component, the same shape as the shared app-modal it already mirrors structurally. Genuinely reduces config-manager.scss's own anyComponentStyle count; costs a new component file and a review of whether it duplicates app-modal enough to reuse it instead — a design-system question this task cannot answer alone.

Raise config-manager's own anyComponentStyle budget via a per-file Angular budget override (angular.json supports per-path budgets), accepting it as a structurally large screen (7 sections, a full CRUD editor) rather than forcing parity with the other three. Cheap and immediate; weakens the blanket 8 kB rule ADR-0041 §7 states, and needs a decision on whether that is acceptable system-wide precedent before T344 flips the budget to an error.

Leave it over budget and scope T344 to exclude config-manager (or delay T344 until a later, separately-scoped cleanup). No new work now; T344 as currently written ('T343: all four screens under budget first') would need its own acceptance text amended to match, or it cannot be marked done.
decisions_needed.recommendation: Option 1 (extract the modal) is the most consistent with this phase's own diagnosis — ADR-0041 §Context: '96% of the stylesheet volume is per-screen code that no other screen can reuse', and a full create-user modal is exactly that. It is also the only option that does not touch ADR-0041 §7's budget rule itself. It is a new component, though, which this task is not authorized to create unilaterally.
